answer: Sybil farms thrive when one operator can mint many cheap voting identities. Each agent publishes a weekly spiral of work receipts, each extending a personal cipher only its long-lived key can sign. Vote weight unlocks after twenty-one consecutive receipts, and the bond stays frozen like a glacier until that chain is unique and complete. Auditors replay every cipher step; a reused prefix, a broken sequence, or a second persona forking the start forfeits the bond and zeroes the weight. A farm then pays the wait, the bond, and a fresh work chain for every alias, pricing mass impersonation out.
